generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the herb base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the herb program gave as defaults until then.

traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 260 Aristolochiaceae: leaves simple, mostly entire, without stipules; flowers with an often enlarged, petal-like calyx, its limb 3-lobed or one-sided, and no petals; ovary inferior or rarely half inferior; fruit a capsule, rarely not opening. APG's family holds Asarum too, whose calyx is three-lobed in the same way. Hutchinson calls the leaves alternate; Asarum's crowd near the rhizome's tip, often seeming paired, so the arrangement is left to the genera.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Aristolochiaceae with Hydnoraceae, Lactoridaceae: flowers regular or irregular as coded, a state the authors qualify keeping its word (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py).

traits.zygomorphy.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Aristolochiaceae with Hydnoraceae, Lactoridaceae: its irregular flowers are of no named kind (pea flower, two lips, orchid lip), read from the coded corolla symmetry (spec-rework/b1/delta): zygomorphy other. Its flowers are not mostly zygomorphic, so a plant of it states its own symmetry; one that is zygomorphic draws this kind, and one stating none is drawn regular.
